title: Funds returning to their origin through a chain of counterparties
definition: A sequence of transfers in which value leaves an account and returns to it, or to an account with a common owner, after passing through one or more unrelated counterparties. The indicator measures the return of value to the origin within a stated window.
evidence_to_cite: the full chain of transfers, each leg cited by its own source id
the ownership or control relationship between the endpoints
the stated commercial reason for each leg
benign_explanations: A group treasury that sweeps funds between operating accounts daily.
A merchant that refunds a deposit to the original payment method.
A payment processor that returns a chargeback or a settlement adjustment.
A business lending money to itself through a subsidiary for a documented reason.

sources.citation: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, money laundering offences as summarised in the FinCrime regulatory index; the indicator is a behavioural measure.
